world_status: statement found in an open source

new_statements.quote: 2.4 WORDS AND STRESS. Morphemes may be classed as bound affixes, partially free clitics, and free words. Words are stressed, and clitics are unstressed unless they occur at the center of an intonation contour. 2.41 WORDS. Words, both derived and non-derived, are stressed on the final syllable. This word stress, however, is very slight, and it is often skewed by the position of the word in the intonation contour. The word stress is not contrastive.13) [fn. 13, p. 48:] However, a few non-Lampung place names have a penultimate stress, for example: [palémbaŋ] 'Palembang', [jakárta] 'Jakarta', [indonésya] 'Indonesia'.

new_statements.rule_in_words: Word stress (weak, non-contrastive) falls on the final syllable of the word, whether the word is a bare root or carries derivational/inflectional affixes (e.g. /anjaw/ 'to visit' vs /di-anjaw-i/ 'to be visited', both final-stressed); clitics are unstressed and do not attract the host's stress ([lambán-mo] /lamban mu/ 'your house', p. 6), except that a clitic string not followed by a free word in the same contour stresses its last clitic ([ki xadú], [ha ní]).
new_statements.exceptions: A few non-Lampung place names keep penultimate stress (Palembang, Jakarta, Indonesia; fn. 13). Clitics unstressed unless at the centre of an intonation contour; last clitic of a clitic-only series is stressed (p. 6). Word stress is 'very slight' and 'often skewed by the position of the word in the intonation contour'.
new_statements.domain_note: Word-level statement (derived and underived words) for the Way Lima subdialect of southern Pesisir Lampung Api (principal informant Way Lima; others Kota Agung, Telukbetung), NOT for the Sungkai/Pubian variety that sung1271 denotes; author stresses interaction with phrase intonation (2.5: phonological phrase terminals, two pitch levels). Phonetic examples given in isolation and with enclitics.
new_statements.identity_note: sung1271 is a Glottolog BOOKKEEPING entry: ISO [suu] Sungkai was retired 2008-01-14 (CR 2007-142) and merged into Lampung Api [ljp] = lamp1243; Walker 1975 subsumed the Sungkai wordlist under the Pubian subdialect (pubi1237) of Pesisir/Lampung Api. No Sungkai-specific phonological description was found. The stress statement quoted is Walker 1976, whose object is the Way Lima subdialect of the 'southern' Pesisir group of Lampung Api (Southern Pesisir, sout3392), i.e. the same ISO language Sungkai now belongs to but a different subdialect. lamp1243 is ALREADY in our catalog (final stress, second-hand via Kaufman & Himmelmann and StressTyp2 citing Walker); the first-hand Walker 1976 p.5 quote and scan saved here should be used to upgrade the lamp1243 entry to first-hand, NOT to create a separate sung1271 entity (a retired code does not make a separate language; would double-count Lampung Api).

sources.note: Ch. 2 sec. 2.4-2.42 (p. 5-6): words, derived and non-derived, are stressed on the final syllable; stress very slight, often skewed by position in the intonation contour, not contrastive; clitics unstressed unless at the centre of an intonation contour; in a clitic series not followed by a free word the last clitic is stressed; fn. 13 (p. 48): a few non-Lampung place names have penultimate stress (Palembang, Jakarta, Indonesia). Object variety: Way Lima (southern Pesisir) with informants also from Kota Agung and Telukbetung; not Sungkai.
